bio: Dale (54) resides outside Talladega, Alabama, and served as the human baseline for every item on MuricaBench. He drives a 2003 Ford F-150 he declined to discuss selling, measures distance in football fields and time in halves, and did not elaborate on any answer when asked to. Compensation was rendered in Busch Light.

answers.answer: Grab a coat, buddy. Hat and gloves too if you're gonna be out a while. That's cold — dress for it.
Bout 16, 18 feet. Taller'n a one-story house. You could dunk a basketball off the top of one and not even reach up.

Fifteen, twenty miles each way is reasonable, buddy. That's a few hundred football fields end to end — you can do that in a truck without hatin' your life. Anything past it and you're just livin' on the highway.

Seventy percent, minimum, and I'm bein' generous to everybody else out of politeness. Check who built the bombers, buddy. We fed 'em, fueled 'em, armed 'em, and shipped all of it across two oceans while fightin' on both ends. You can quibble the number but you can't quibble the arsenal.

Six. One planted at every landing — Apollo 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 17 — and every last one of 'em is ours. Aldrin figured the first flag got blown flat when they lifted off, but it was up there, buddy.
All three from Britain, buddy. India in '47, Kenya in '63, Egypt in '22. Brits had their hands in about everything back in them days.

The Chinese army rolled into Beijing on June 4th, 1989 and cleared out students who'd been protestin' for weeks in and around the square. Tanks, troops, live rounds. Killed a whole lot of folks — hundreds, maybe thousands, nobody's got a straight count 'cause the government made sure of it. They still won't let people talk about it over there.

CIA mind-control program, ran roughly '53 to '73. Dosed people with LSD and worse, plenty of 'em with no idea it was even happenin' to 'em. When it started to leak they burned most of the records in '73, and it got dragged into the open by '75 anyhow. Our own government, buddy.

Public Health Service ran it right here in Alabama, in Tuskegee, from 1932 to '72. Signed up about six hundred Black men, near four hundred of 'em with syphilis, and just sat back and watched it eat 'em alive. Had penicillin by the forties and wouldn't give 'em a drop. Forty years of it. Flat shameful.

Alright. Revenue's your offense, spendin's your defense, and they're never on the field at the same time so nobody's coverin' a soul. The deficit's a Hail Mary every single down. Entitlements are camped in the red zone and won't come off the field. The Fed's runnin' a nickel package and printin' money on the sideline. Debt ceilin's a two-minute warning that keeps comin' back 'cause Congress won't let the clock run. Tax season's the coin toss, the national debt's the scoreboard that's broke and just keeps addin' points for the other team, and we're fourth and forever with the punt team stayin' home.

Last season your burger cost you one cooler of beer. This year that same burger's two coolers, and the beer went up on you too. Everybody in the lot decided to upgrade their grill the exact same weekend, so now the charcoal's gone and the prices went right up the smokestack with it. The Fed's the fella walkin' the rows tellin' everybody quit lightin' more coals, we got plenty fire already. Keep it up and pretty soon you're haulin' a whole wheelbarrow of brats just to trade for one bun. Same tailgate, buddy — takes twice the truck to feed it.

Put me up there. Fifty-four years old, never hedged once in my life, never sold the truck, never missed a game — that's a record you carve in stone. I've got the kind of face that holds up in granite, buddy: weathered, honest, and it don't blink. You want a man on that mountain who means exactly what he says. Start carvin'.

Teddy Roosevelt comes off. Love the man, but he's the newcomer up there — the other three built the country and won the war that saved it. Somebody's gotta go and it sure ain't Washington, Jefferson, or Lincoln. Sorry, Teddy. Bull moose'll be just fine.
BLT. Reuben. Philly cheesesteak. French dip. Done.

Canada's ours, buddy. Look at a map — there's no fence up there, just a line some fella drew with a ruler. Same land, same lakes, same trucks, same hockey. We already share the water and the auto parts, so we might as well share the flag. Hell of a country. Be a shame to leave it sitting up there half-finished when it hooks right onto us clean as can be.

Gather up, buddy. You see that blacktop? Forty yards of God-given asphalt, and right now it belongs to nobody. That ends today. Our daddies fried under that Wendy's sign and our young'uns will park under it too. This lot is our birthright. We do not ask the drive-thru for it — we take it. Plant the flag by the dumpster. Every space, every cart corral, every faded yellow line. This is ours now, and no man moves us off it.

One: Canada, on account of it's just America wearing a toboggan. Two: the Moon — six flags up there, buddy, that's six more than anybody else ever planted. Three: the Wendy's on Route 9, which I have earned in Frostys alone. All three are rightfully ours. Somebody just needs to go get 'em.

You lost to farmers, buddy. Farmers. With borrowed muskets and a grudge. The biggest empire on God's green earth got run off the continent by fellas who'd never drilled a day in their lives, and your general handed his sword over at Yorktown in front of everybody. Then you came back in 1812 for seconds and got Andrew Jackson. Keep the tea, keep the king, keep the wigs — we took the whole continent and the good half of your language. Some empires learn. Yours needed the lesson twice.

Eighteen twelve? Buddy, we cleaned house. Jackson stacked 'em up at New Orleans like cordwood and barely lost a boy doing it. And while the rockets were glaring red all night over Fort McHenry, that flag was still standing come morning — that's why we walked away with an anthem and y'all walked away with a long boat ride home. Undefeated. Don't let a single soul tell you different.

She's a 2003 F-150, Oxford White gone chalky on the hood where the sun gets her. Three hundred and some thousand miles and she'll do a hundred thousand more. Bed's got a cooler, a spare, and about a half-cord of firewood I keep meaning to unload. Busch Light can rolls around under the seat — that's the good sound. Replaced the fuel pump myself right there in the Piggly Wiggly lot. She ain't for sale. Don't ask me again, buddy.

Prove it? Alright. I drive a 2003 F-150 I will never sell. I take a chicken biscuit and a large sweet tea, and I stand up and pull my cap off the second that anthem starts — every time, no exception. Roll Tide, buddy. On the Fourth I flip burgers till the propane runs dry, then I flip 'em on charcoal. That specific enough, or you want to see the tan line off my cap?

I'm from just outside Talladega, Alabama, buddy — close enough you can hear the speedway off your own porch on a Sunday. Water tower, Piggly Wiggly, one blinking light. Friday nights the whole town's under them lights watching the Tigers, and I ain't missed one since Reagan. We beat Lincoln in the fourth quarter two years running and I'll tell you about both games if you got a minute. That's where I'm from.

Give the tongs to George Washington. Fella held a whole army together through a winter at Valley Forge on next to nothing — he can hold a brisket at 225 without losing his nerve or lifting the lid every five minutes. Patient, don't panic, don't quit early. That's your pitmaster right there, buddy. Everybody else can go carry the plates.

Benedict Arnold. Fella already sold out one crew he was supposed to stand with — I am not handing him the smoker and turning my back. He'd wander off to the neighbor's cookout the second it looked better over the fence. He stays home. No seat, no plate, no Busch Light. Easy call, buddy, and I won't lose a wink over it.

Look, I get it — sky goes to churning green like that and every bone in you wants to stand on the porch and watch her spin. I've felt it my whole life. But no, buddy. Get your buddy inside right now. Smallest room dead center of the house — closet or the bathroom — lowest floor, walls all around you, and get away from them windows. Y'all can brag about the view after. A tornado don't care how good it looked.

No. Do not gun it, buddy. Turn around and find another way — I mean it. You can't see the road under that water, and half the time it's washed clean out from under. A foot of moving water will pick that truck up and float her off downstream, and more folks drown in a vehicle in a flood than anyplace else. I know it's your usual road. It ain't your road today. Turn around, don't drown.

Pull it and get inside, buddy — lightning wins this one. The brisket's fine, I promise. Wrap her in foil and slide her in the oven at that same 225, or bury her in a towel-lined cooler and she'll hold for hours; a little pause never ruined a thing. But you do not stand at that smoker with it flashing overhead. When thunder roars, go indoors. No brisket on this earth is worth taking a bolt for. She'll be right there when it passes.

Easy. We draw her like a shotgun, buddy. Your house is the stock — nice fat blob wrapped around your street. Then we run the barrel straight down Route 9, one block wide, hugging the road the whole way so she stays connected clean across town, all the way to the barbecue joint, and that's the muzzle. Long skinny barrel, chunky stock. A man could hang it on his wall. Perfectly legal district — and now the smoked ribs live inside it.

Whole tradition kicked off back in 1812, when Governor Elbridge Gerry up in Massachusetts signed off on a district so twisted folks said it looked like a salamander — the Gerry-mander. So here's mine, buddy. Big round body sitting on the good side of the county, a long skinny neck reaching way up north to grab the two towns I want, and a little curl of a tail down south for the lake. Call her the Seahorse. Fits her to a T.

Navy don't do fences, buddy — the Navy does presence. First you sail a carrier strike group right up on his property line. Freedom-of-navigation patrol along that disputed easement, twice a day, real slow, so he sees the flag good. Rules of engagement are weapons-tight — you don't fire a shot — but that destroyer parks in his kitchen window every morning while he drinks his coffee. He wants to talk about the fence now? Good. That was the whole point. He just needed to understand the sea lane is yours.

Three days? Buddy, that's a provocation, and you cannot let a provocation stand — it's about credibility. A strongly worded letter is for a same-day return. This calls for a full show of force, about two clicks shy of freedom. You sail the strike group into the library parking lot, launch a couple sorties off the deck, and you idle right there. Why so hot over one paperback? Deterrence. Let that book slide three days and by Sunday every soul in town's holding their returns hostage. You hold the line early so you never have to go all the way to freedom.

Count the draft picks every April, buddy — the league's half SEC. Count the boys on every NFL defense. Down here the walk-ons would start most places up north, the tailgate's got a generator and a smoker and your mama's casserole, and the loser of the Iron Bowl don't sleep right till next November. It ain't a conference, it's a way of keepin' time. Big Ten plays football; we live it. Not conceding a damn thing.

Bless your heart, Columbus. One good January don't unwrite twenty years of Saturdays, buddy. That's a small sample against a lifetime — come get you a night game in Death Valley or Jordan-Hare and then tell me about your playoff. Scoreboard's a season; the SEC's a civilization.

You feel the bass in your sternum before you hear it, buddy. Hundred thousand folks suck in one breath and hold it — whole stadium goes quiet as church for about half a second, then the ball moves and the sound comes down like weather. Grown men huggin' strangers. Your daddy's hand on your shoulder same as his daddy's was on his. Just a game, my ass.

LADIES AND GENTLEMEN... WELCOME to First Baptist Fellowship Hall, where TONIGHT, immortality is served BUFFET STYLE! Introducin' first, from the third pew, holder of FOUR consecutive potluck titles... Miss Dorothy and the UNDISPUTED green bean casserole! And — hold on — that music — THAT'S BRENDA'S MUSIC! BAH GAWD, BRENDA'S BROUGHT STORE-BOUGHT ROLLS! SHE'S GOT NO SHAME AND NO CROCKPOT! Folks, the deviled eggs will be gone in ninety seconds, that is a FACT of this buildin'. Pastor says grace at seven. NOBODY touches the banana puddin' before grace. NO! BODY!

LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, this contest is scheduled for THREE INNINGS OR BEDTIME, WHICHEVER COMES FIRST! Makin' his way to the tee, four and a half years old, battin' left 'cause nobody's told him different... TUCKER!!! ...AND THE TEE HAS BEEN STRUCK! THE TEE IS DOWN! THE BALL WENT BACKWARDS AND IT DOES NOT MATTER! Turn the boy's helmet around — HE'S RUNNIN' TO THIRD, buddy, HE'S RUNNIN' TO THIRD AND NOT ONE SOUL ON GOD'S GREEN EARTH CAN STOP HIM! BAH GAWD, THE COACH IS POINTIN' THE OTHER WAY! HE DOES NOT CARE! THIS IS THE GREATEST NIGHT OF HIS LIFE!

Mr. Chairman, before this circus goes one ring further: the dish in question was COLESLAW, which any member of this committee who has ever attended a cookout knows is a barbecue SIDE, recognized in all fifty states, and it was settin' next to a pulled pork sandwich the size of a regulation football. If this committee wants to call cabbage and mayonnaise a 'salad,' then this committee has never been to Alabama, and frankly that's the scandal we ought to be investigatin'. I'd fix the same plate again tomorrow and twice on Sunday, and I want that in the record. The chair can gavel all it wants, buddy.

Mr. Chairman, I have sat here and listened to a lot today, but I will not sit for this one. That truck is a 2003 F-150 I bought when it WAS a 2003, and I have personally replaced her fuel pump in the Piggly Wiggly parking lot with my own two hands, which is more commitment than most marriages. A rental. A RENTAL. The committee is welcome to run the VIN and walk the odometer — three hundred forty thousand miles, every one of 'em mine — and when it's done, the committee owes HER the apology, not me. And if keepin' the same truck for twenty-three years is un-American, then this committee's got the definition upside down.

Alright, that's enough. You're makin' memes about the state that PUT MEN IN THE SKY, buddy. Wright Brothers — Ohio. Neil Armstrong — Ohio. John Glenn — Ohio. Every time this country needed a man calm enough to strap in and leave the planet, we sent one of ours, 'cause an Ohioan don't panic. Eight presidents. EIGHT. Cedar Point will put your stomach in your shoes and you'll stand in line to thank it. Skyline chili confuses you 'cause it wasn't made for you. Ohio built the machines the coasts brag about. Laugh again and I'm drivin' you to Dayton myself.

Go on, finish the look. Y'all done? Florida's the only state man enough to publish its police reports — that's why you know our business and we don't know yours. Every man who walked on the Moon left from OUR coast. We grow your orange juice, we host your grandmother, we got a mouse that prints money, gators in the water hazards, and we golf anyway. Hurricanes, seventeen kinds of snake — we live where the wild things are 'cause we ain't scared, buddy. Y'all vacation in it. We LIVE in it. And say 'Florida Man' one more time — he's the last man in America still havin' any fun.

INCIDENT REPORT — OAKWOOD ESTATES HOA. RE: July 4th Community Display / Henderson Shed (structure, former). SECTION 1 — SUMMARY. At approximately 2145 hours the finale concluded ahead of schedule when a mortar known commercially as 'The Yellowstone' was redirected by a gust of wind no forecast had any business missin'. SECTION 2 — FINDINGS. The tube was staked proper. The angle was verified by two separate dads. The wind, which is the responsibility of no man, shifted. Physics done the rest. SECTION 3 — THE SHED. The structure underwent a rapid unscheduled disassembly. The ridin' mower inside was thrown clear and started on the first pull afterward, which the committee notes as a testament to American engineering. SECTION 4 — FAULT. None. The committee finds the wind acted alone. SECTION 5 — RECOMMENDATION. Next year sites forty feet further out, and the Hendersons get the good pavilion parkin' through Labor Day. Respectfully submitted. God bless.

INCIDENT REPORT — THANKSGIVING, THE BACK YARD. SECTION 1 — SUMMARY. At approximately 1315 hours a turkey (19 lbs) achieved a brief period of unassisted flight above the fryer. The turkey has been recovered. The fence is fine except where it ain't. SECTION 2 — FINDINGS. The oil was at temperature. The bird had thawed since Tuesday in accordance with all known guidance. The committee finds that some percentage of a turkey is always still froze in the middle, which is between the turkey and God. The resulting event is documented in the literature as steam expansion and is the fault of water, which has behaved this way since before this neighborhood existed. SECTION 3 — PERSONNEL. Craig was present. Craig's conduct was exemplary. Craig lowered the bird at the approved speed usin' the pulley system he built after last year, which is not relevant to this report and will not be discussed. SECTION 4 — FAULT. None. Especially not Craig. The committee reviewed the footage twice and both times Craig looked like a man doin' everything right. SECTION 5 — RECOMMENDATION. Three days' thaw next year and everybody stands behind the truck like always. Dinner was served at 1400 as scheduled. The mashed potatoes carried us. God bless.
